ENGINEERING ASSESSMENT REPORT
Date of Inspection: March 5, 2026
Property: 321 Elm Street, Tulsa OK

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY:
This residential property was inspected following a severe storm event on February 15, 2026 that produced wind gusts of 75 mph and quarter-sized hail. Our inspection identified wind uplift damage on the west-facing slope and scattered hail impact marks on soft metal components. The shingle system shows evidence of both wind creasing and hail-related granule displacement.

FINDINGS:
The west-facing slope exhibited multiple lifted tabs and creased tabs consistent with wind uplift forces. Seal strip adhesion was compromised on approximately 30% of shingles on this elevation. We observed peel back damage on three ridge cap shingles.

Hail impact marks were noted on aluminum vents and the HVAC condenser unit. Minor granule displacement was observed on shingle surfaces, but no mat fracture or brittle fracture was identified. The hail damage is cosmetic only and does not affect waterproofing integrity.

No test square analysis was performed. Hand seal testing was not conducted. Wind speed correlation with damage patterns was not analyzed.

CONCLUSION:
The tab lifting and creasing are attributed to normal aging and wear and tear of the seal strip adhesive. The shingle manufacturer rates these shingles for 110 mph wind resistance; therefore, the 75 mph winds should not have caused the observed conditions. The hail impacts are cosmetic damage that does not warrant replacement. We recommend routine maintenance and individual tab re-sealing.
